task: For this synthetic writing exercise, use the fictional reporting notes to write a business news story for a general newspaper audience. Write from this reporting snapshot as of April 24, 2025. Include a headline. Target 450 to 650 words. Follow AP style.

facts.text: Vantage Market Group announced it will close 23 of its 87 supermarkets across Ohio, Indiana, Kentucky, and West Virginia, citing sustained financial losses and an inability to compete on price.
Vantage reported a net loss of $47 million in the fourth quarter of 2024, its third consecutive quarterly loss.
The 23 stores employ approximately 1,800 workers; about 1,100 are full-time employees.
Workers at 14 of the 23 closing stores are represented by United Food and Commercial Workers Local 880.
Local 880 president David Osei said: "Our members are losing jobs right before summer, without the notice they are legally owed."

Osei said the union planned to file a federal court complaint seeking WARN Act remedies, alleging Vantage failed to give the required advance notice. No complaint had been filed as of the reporting snapshot.
Vantage CEO Gregory Patton said: "We cannot ask our shareholders to fund losses indefinitely in markets where we no longer have a viable path to profitability."
Patton said the company lost market share in rural and small-city markets to Walmart, Aldi, and a Kroger subsidiary that has expanded aggressively in the region over the past four years.
Closures are scheduled to begin April 30, 2025, and conclude by June 15, 2025.
Two of the closing stores — one in Millfield, Ohio, and one in Dunning, Kentucky — are the only full-service grocery stores within 12 miles of their respective communities.
Local officials in Millfield and Dunning said they had not been notified before the announcement; Millfield Mayor Roger Callahan called the closure "a gut punch to a town that's already struggling."
Vantage carries approximately $210 million in long-term debt; the company plans to sell or sublease its store properties to reduce the debt load.

WARN generally requires covered employers to give 60 days' advance written notice for qualifying plant closings or mass layoffs; coverage thresholds and exceptions matter. The union asserts that the affected stores qualify and no exception excuses shorter notice. The packet contains no court finding on coverage or liability.
Vantage reported revenue of $1.42 billion in fiscal year 2024, down from $1.61 billion in 2022.
Patton said the company expects to return to profitability with the remaining 64 stores by the end of fiscal year 2026, but did not provide specific projections.
Workers who spoke with reporters outside the Millfield store described learning of the closure through an all-hands meeting that morning; none said they had received written notice.
The company has not identified any buyers for the store properties.
Vantage was founded in 1978 and at its peak operated 140 stores across six states.

The packet supplies no collective agreement or company severance policy for the non-unionized stores. Interviewed workers at those stores said Thursday that they had received no severance information.
The company's stock fell 9.4 percent Thursday on news of the closures.
